Title: Understand Solidatus models
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-6.5/models/understand-solidatus-models
Content: A common definition of a model is “a representation of some aspect of the world that is based on simplifying assumptions.” This definition fits Solidatus models in some respects but not others.

Like all models, Solidatus models are representations “of” something, usually a complex technical infrastructure that enables data processing, analysis, and reporting.

Unlike other models, Solidatus models are designed to ingest and record the full complexity of what they represent without simplification. Once this complexity is ingested, models become both storehouses of fine-grained information about target data landscapes and visual, interactive tools that make it possible to dissect and simplify complexity.

Given their flexible structure and open meaning, Solidatus models can represent anything from rail networks to supply chains to the application of regulations to data systems and pipelines.

In all of these cases, models are tools that make it possible to capture critical information and easily answer urgent questions about complex technical systems and processes.

Visit the pages in this section for an introduction to the composition of Solidatus models, the two types of model (Lineage and Reference), model building principles, and typical use-cases.
Title: Quick-start guide
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-6.5/get-started/quick-start-guide
Content: Solidatus models are many things at once: explorable visualizations, analytical tools, and queryable storehouses of metadata. Their core purpose is to make complex data landscapes understandable, governable, and transparent.

Simplify and analyse complex data landscapes

Built-in features like filters and display rules transform technical diagrams into powerful analytical tools that simplify complex landscapes and highlight key information.

In the Solidatus platform, models serve as the foundation for user-friendly Data Domains that make lineage and metadata captured in models discoverable and accessible to business users.

Title: Solidatus basics for domain explorers
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-2026.2/data-domains/explore-data-domains/solidatus-basics-for-domain-explorers
Content: Solidatus Data Domains are built on top of Solidatus models, which are visualisation tools used to capture and store data lineage and metadata for data that exists in an organisation’s data ecosystem.

All information that surfaces in a Data Domain originally comes from a set of models that are published to the domain.

Data Domains are portals into information stored in models. They provide tools to help you understand and visualise data lineage within meaningful business contexts.

Information in a Data Domain can only be edited in the original source models, not directly in the domain itself.

If you have a question about something you find in a Data Domain, or if you have a suggestion for editing content, contact the Domain Owner. Owners of a domain can consult the original source models or contact Owners of the original models, to make necessary changes.
